originality.rationale: The sharp minimum for total nonzero-weight edges across models realizing every bounded-depth type, its exact closed formula for arbitrary finite Heyting A, and characterization of all simultaneous state-and-edge minimizers were not found in the primary works or published research-record comparisons. Generic terminal sequences and canonical universal models are prior art (Lin--Liau 2022) and expressly not claimed as new. An older implicit resource-optimization corollary remains a material risk.
residual_risks: A generic coalgebraic terminal-sequence model may implicitly be chosen with the same minimum edge supports; the new claim is the explicit sharp optimization and equality theorem, not terminal-sequence existence.
Unindexed earlier many-valued modal logic, universal-model, or automata literature could formulate the same resource optimum under alternate terms.
Some adjacent published research records are summaries rather than fully inspected papers; no claim of global uniqueness is made.

value.rationale: The optimization is the natural total positive-transition cost of a single semantic test model representing every depth-bounded weighted modal theory. Its all-depth closed formula is sharp and simultaneously realizable with the minimum state budget, and the equality case identifies all extremal transition architectures. It goes beyond an arbitrary numerical instance or per-formula model bound.
